title: AMP Manifest
description: Unified semantic schema for the Agent Manifest Protocol ecosystem. Version 1.0 captures AMP expansions, identities, connectors, agent spec, and Adaptive Card flashcards. Version 1.1 extends a conforming manifest so it can declare and version Agent Client Protocol (stable v1 and draft v2), Activity Protocol (provisional 3.4 baseline with optional v5), MCP 2.0 (2026-07-28 streamable HTTP and stateless MCP) with 2025-06-18 backward compatibility, and MCP Apps (SEP-1865).

version.description: AMP spec version of this manifest document. Omit or use 1.0.0 for the original shape. Use 1.1.0 when declaring interop protocols.

protocol.description: AMP expansions implemented by this manifest. Interop wire protocols (ACP, Activity, MCP, MCP Apps) are declared and versioned under `protocols`, not here.

semantic.description: Unified semantic layer for schemas consumed by AMP systems.

adaptiveCardVersions.description: Adaptive Card 2.1 is required and 1.6 compatibility is retained.

mcpUiApps.description: Legacy string names remain valid. Object entries declare SEP-1865 MCP Apps (`ui://` resources, `text/html;profile=mcp-app`).

implementationInfo.description: Implementation metadata exchanged during ACP initialize or MCP _meta clientInfo/serverInfo.

id.description: Every agent has a required identifier.

tools.description: Tool names as strings remain valid. Object entries may attach MCP input schemas and SEP-1865 `_meta.ui` linkage.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 input schema as used by MCP tools/list.

_meta.description: MCP tool metadata. Prefer `_meta.ui.resourceUri` (SEP-1865). The flat `_meta["ui/resourceUri"]` key is deprecated.

resourceUri.description: UI resource for rendering tool results. MUST use the ui:// scheme.

visibility.description: Who can access this tool. Default in SEP-1865 is ["model", "app"].

agentProtocolBindings.description: Per-agent bindings to declared interop protocols. Version matrices live on `protocols`; this object points the agent at concrete endpoints and roles.

endpoint.description: Programmatically addressable location where the Agent or channel receives activities.

channelId.description: Activity Protocol channelId, for example msteams or webchat.

endpoint.description: Single MCP HTTP endpoint path, for example https://example.com/mcp.

mcpAppRef.description: SEP-1865 MCP App UI resource referenced from the AMP UI surface.

uri.description: Unique UI resource identifier. MUST use the ui:// scheme.

toolName.description: Tool whose `_meta.ui.resourceUri` points at this resource.

mcpAppMimeType.description: Initial MCP Apps content type. Other types are reserved for future extensions.

mcpUiCsp.description: Content Security Policy origins declared by an MCP App. Hosts MUST NOT allow undeclared domains.

mcpUiPermissions.description: Sandbox Permission Policy features requested by an MCP App.

interopProtocols.description: Versioned declarations of interop protocols a conforming AMP agent, app, or API speaks. Existing AMP expansions stay in `protocol`.

acpProtocolVersion.description: ACP initialize `protocolVersion` integer. 1 is the current stable wire version. 2 is draft.

acpDeclaration.description: Agent Client Protocol declaration. Stable v1 plus optional draft v2 (protocolVersion 2). See https://agentclientprotocol.com.

supportedProtocolVersions.description: ACP `initialize` protocolVersion integers this peer can negotiate. Implementers SHOULD keep v1 when adding draft v2.

authMethods.description: Authentication methods advertised in ACP initialize. A non-empty list requires auth/login and auth/logout (v2) or authenticate (v1).

transports.description: ACP transports. stdio is the stable default. Streamable HTTP and WebSocket are draft / RFD.

status.description: stdio is stable. streamable-http and websocket are draft (ACP Transports WG / RFD).

acpV1Profile.description: Stable ACP v1 profile. protocolVersion 1. Capabilities map to AgentCapabilities / ClientCapabilities from the v1 schema.

schema.description: Published ACP v1 JSON Schema URI or release artifact, for example schema/v1/schema.json.

methods.description: Baseline and optional v1 methods this peer implements.

mcpCapabilities.description: ACP v1 MCP-over-session transports the agent can launch.

acpV2Profile.description: Draft ACP v2 profile. protocolVersion 2. Breaking session and update semantics; do not treat as a drop-in for v1.

schema.description: Published ACP v2 JSON Schema URI or release artifact (v2.0.0-alphaX).

agentCapabilities.description: ACP v2 initialize AgentCapabilities. Session surfaces nest prompt and MCP transports.

features.description: Draft v2 behavioral surfaces from the v2 RFDs and migration guide.

activityDeclaration.description: Microsoft Agents Activity Protocol. Provisional 3.4 is the required baseline. Schema v5 (payload-first envelope, v: "5") is an optional extension that MUST coexist with 3.4 during transition.

baseline.description: Provisional Activity Protocol 3.4 is the AMP baseline. Receivers that omit `v` or send a non-"5" value are treated as v3.4.

supportedVersions.description: Declared Activity Protocol versions. MUST include the 3.4 baseline. "5" opts into the v5 envelope.

activityTypes.description: v3.4 activity type values this peer understands. Application-layer types MAY also be listed as additional strings via customActivityTypes.

activityV34Profile.description: Provisional 3.4 baseline profile. Activities are a flat JSON object with a type discriminator; channels master id and timestamp.

serializableJson.description: A2001: activities MUST be serializable to JSON (RFC 4627).

unknownFieldsAccepted.description: A2005: receivers MUST accept fields they do not understand.

activityV5Extension.description: Optional Activity Protocol Schema v5 extension (Microsoft Agents issue #472). Minimal symmetric envelope: all modalities live in `payload`; typed `entities` are metadata only; correlation uses `relatesTo`. Senders MUST set `v` to "5".

marker.description: Normative `v` field value that triggers v5 schema parsing.

payloadContentTypes.description: Declared payload.contentType values, for example text/plain, text/markdown, application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive.

entitiesMetadataOnly.description: v5 typed entities carry metadata only (capabilities, locale, delegation, delivery hints).

relatesToGraph.description: Replies, updates, deletes, tool calls, and streaming correlate via relatesTo rather than separate callbacks.

mcpProtocolVersion.description: MCP protocol revision date. 2026-07-28 is MCP 2.0 (stateless / streamable). 2025-06-18 is the required backward-compat revision.

mcpEra.description: modern = 2026-07-28+ per-request _meta, no initialize. legacy = 2025-11-25 and earlier initialize handshake. dual-era = both on the same endpoint.

mcpDeclaration.description: Model Context Protocol declaration. Prefer 2026-07-28 (MCP 2.0): stateless core, Streamable HTTP POST-only, request-scoped SSE, server/discover, MRTR. Dual-era peers MUST also list 2025-06-18 for initialize / Mcp-Session-Id compatibility.

stateless.description: true when the peer speaks MCP 2.0 request/response without initialize or Mcp-Session-Id (SEP-2575, SEP-2567).

resultTypes.description: 2026-07-28 results carry required resultType. Clients MUST treat omitted resultType from earlier servers as complete.

extensions.description: Optional MCP extensions advertised in capabilities.extensions. Keys MUST be prefixed identifiers.

io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks.description: Official tasks extension (SEP-2663). Moved out of the MCP 2.0 core.

cacheableResults.description: SEP-2549 cache hints required on 2026-07-28 list/read results.

stdio.description: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a client-launched subprocess. On 2026-07-28, clients MAY probe with server/discover before falling back to initialize.

httpSse.description: Deprecated HTTP+SSE transport from protocol version 2024-11-05 (SEP-2596). Dual-era servers MAY keep it for older clients.

mcpStreamableHttp.description: Streamable HTTP binding. 2026-07-28: single POST endpoint, no GET stream, no Mcp-Session-Id, request-scoped SSE, required Mcp-Method / Mcp-Name / MCP-Protocol-Version headers. 2025-06-18: POST+GET, optional sessions, initialize handshake.

endpoint.description: Single MCP HTTP endpoint, for example https://example.com/mcp.

mode.description: stateless = 2026-07-28 POST-only. session = 2025-06-18 optional Mcp-Session-Id. dual-era = both detection paths on one origin.

httpMethods.description: 2026-07-28 requires POST only. 2025-06-18 uses POST and optional GET (SSE listen) plus optional DELETE (session end).

headers.description: Required or optional Streamable HTTP headers for the declared revisions.

name.description: Required on 2026-07-28 tools/call, resources/read, and prompts/get.

sessionId.description: Mcp-Session-Id for 2025-06-18 sessionful servers. MUST be null/omitted for stateless 2026-07-28.

sessions.description: false for 2026-07-28 (protocol-level sessions removed). true when a 2025-06-18 peer may mint Mcp-Session-Id.

getStream.description: Standalone GET SSE stream. Removed in 2026-07-28; used by 2025-06-18.

lastEventId.description: SSE resumability via Last-Event-ID. Removed in 2026-07-28; optional in 2025-06-18.

originValidation.description: Servers MUST validate Origin to prevent DNS rebinding.

mcpRequestMeta.description: Per-request `_meta` keys for modern MCP (2026-07-28). The HTTP binding also mirrors version into MCP-Protocol-Version.

traceContext.description: W3C Trace Context keys reserved inside _meta (SEP-414).

modern.description: 2026-07-28 methods. server/discover is REQUIRED for servers.

legacy.description: 2025-06-18 and other initialize-era methods retained for dual-era / backward-compat peers.

mcpAppsDeclaration.description: MCP Apps (SEP-1865). Optional MCP extension that delivers interactive HTML UIs via ui:// resources, tool `_meta.ui` linkage, and postMessage JSON-RPC (`ui/initialize`).

specification.description: Stable MCP Apps specification date in modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps.

transport.description: UI iframes speak MCP JSON-RPC to the host over postMessage.
